newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wah Lee says to double China distribution outlets.
newsitem.headline: Wah Lee says to double China distribution outlets.

text.p: Electrical and photographic products distributor Wah Lee Resources Holdings Ltd plans to double its distribution outlets in China to a total of about 80 in two to three years times.
"We plan to increase the distribution outlets in China from the current 40 to about 80 in coming two to three years," said the company's chairman Yeung Kwok Fan in a briefing on Monday.
Wah Lee's finance director Thomas Wong said the company planned to open more outlets in major Chinese coastal cities, such as Shanghai, in southern China.

"We see huge potential in the China market because existing distribution network in southern China had already contributed over HK$800 million turnover," Wong said. "Business potential is huge if we further penetrate into other areas (in China)."
Wah Lee said its turnover jumped to HK$848.84 million for the year ended in June 1996, from HK$676.73 million in 1995 and HK$570.42 in 1994.
Wong also said he expected the company had bright earnings prospects because distribution would be important for overseas manufacturers to enter the China market.
"They (overseas manufacturer) need a distributor who has thorough understanding of the China market, as a bridge to enter or promote their products in China," Wong said.
Wah Lee distributes Mitsubishi air conditioning systems, Thomson audio-visual products and Konica photographic products in China.
Wah Lee offer 70 million new shares at HK$1.00 per share, giving a prospective price to earnings multiple of 6.6 times on a weighted average basis, and 6.76 times on proforma fully-diluted basis.
A warrant will be attached for every five shares subscribed.
The company forecasts its profit after taxation but before extraordinary items of about HK$40 million for the year ending June 30, 1997, up from HK$25.6 million for the year ended in June 1996.
Net proceeds will be used to promote new products, to set up display showrooms across China and to buy a warehouse in Hong Kong. The remaining balance will be for working capital.
The IPO runs from December 31 to January 6 and dealing in the company shares is expected to begin on January 17.
